newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Ecstasy smugglers use Indonesian postal service.
newsitem.headline: Ecstasy smugglers use Indonesian postal service.

text.p: The Indonesian postal service is becoming a major route for drug smuggling into the country, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Tuesday.

"This year alone, at least 115,874 Ecstasy pills and 1.8 kg (four lbs) of heroin have been seized by customs officers at major post offices in the country," Thomas Sugijata, head of prevention and investigation at Indonesia's Customs and Excise, told the newspaper.
He said most drugs were smuggled into Indonesia in packages mailed to fictitious names at addresses in the capital Jakarta, the second city of Surabaya, and Medan in North Sumatra.
"Most of the locals mentioned on the parcels claim to have no idea who the senders are," he said. The newspaper did not say how the smugglers collected the packages.

Earlier this month, customs officials in Semarang, central Java, found 108,290 Ecstasy pills in three packages mailed from Thailand, Pakistan and Hong Kong, in the biggest single drugs haul by Indonesian authorities to date.
However, Sugijata said the county's airports were still the most popular entry way for drug smugglers, with customs agents having seized 239,048 Ecstasy pills at major airports since March this year.
President Suharto warned last week at the opening of a conference on drug abuse that Indonesia was vulnerable to the international drug trade because of its geographical location.
Indonesia, an archipelagic nation of more than 13,000 islands, has had several of high-profile Ecstasy arrests in recent months as the designer drug has become popular among the country's elite.
